# SPEC-013 — DAG-Aware Parallel Dispatch for /ship (M1)

This directory contains the human-readable documentation for the M1 parallel dispatch feature
shipped as part of planr-pipeline v0.11.0.

## What was shipped

The `/planr-pipeline:ship` command previously processed tasks two-at-a-time, bounded by a
per-User-Story structure that ignored whether tasks across different stories were actually
dependent on each other. A twelve-task spec with entirely independent work still dripped through
two concurrent agents at a time, US by US.

M1 replaces that walk (in `DISPATCH_MODE: multi-task` only) with a **wave-based topological
scheduler**. The orchestrator computes a ready frontier across all pending and blocked tasks
simultaneously, groups compatible tasks into a wave, and emits all K `Agent` tool-calls for that
wave in one orchestrator turn. When all K results are back, it recomputes the frontier and repeats
until the queue is empty.

A wave is bounded by two things: a configurable cap (`--max-parallel N`, default 4) and write-set
safety (two tasks that declare overlapping files are never placed in the same wave). This is
layer 1 of a three-layer write-safety model described in detail in
[architecture.md](architecture.md).

## Runtime scope

M1 fan-out is **Claude Code only, multi-task mode only**. Cursor and Codex run
`DISPATCH_MODE: per-task` (one task per invocation, sequential, main tree). The `--max-parallel`
flag has no effect on those runtimes. See [architecture.md](architecture.md) and
`docs/compatibility-matrix.md` for the full matrix.

## Quick reference

```
/planr-pipeline:ship <slug>                   # default: --max-parallel 4
/planr-pipeline:ship <slug> --max-parallel 8  # wider waves
/planr-pipeline:ship <slug> --max-parallel 1  # sequential-equivalent escape hatch
```

The scheduler procedure lives at `procedures/ship-step2-dag-dispatch.md`.
The wave write-safety rule is `docs/rules.md` R11.
The argument parsing lives at `procedures/ship-arguments-and-cost-gate.md` Phase A.
